enriched_description: Three-wheeled human-powered vehicle with one front wheel and two rear wheels. Frame is steel tubing painted in bright colors (red, blue, yellow, green). Front wheel has handlebars for steering. Seat is a molded plastic saddle positioned above the rear axle. Pedals connect directly to the front wheel hub via crank arms. Rear wheels are smaller than the front. Overall length approximately 80-120 cm. Some models have a basket mounted on the handlebars or rear. Chain guard covers the drivetrain on adult models.

Fast sailing vessel with three parallel hulls: a central main hull and two smaller outrigger hulls (amas) connected by crossbeams (akas). Main hull is slender and pointed at both ends, 8-15 meters long. Outrigger hulls are positioned 3-5 meters to each side. Mast rises from the center of the main hull with a large triangular mainsail and jib. Deck is flat and open between the hulls. Hulls are fiberglass or aluminum in white. Rigging lines (sheets, halyards) run along the deck. The wide stance provides exceptional stability at high speeds.

Three-legged support device with legs extending from a central hub. Each leg is adjustable in length via telescoping sections with locking clamps or twist locks. Top features a mounting platform with a pan-tilt head and a 1/4-inch or 3/8-inch screw for attaching cameras or instruments. Legs are aluminum or carbon fiber in black or silver. Spread angle is adjustable via a center column or individual leg locks. Height ranges from 30 cm (tabletop) to 180 cm (full extension). Rubber or spiked feet at the leg ends. Carrying handle on the center column.

Monumental arched gateway structure constructed from stone, marble, or concrete. Central archway is tall (15-50 meters) with a semicircular or pointed opening. Flanking columns or pilasters frame the arch. Decorative reliefs and sculptural panels adorn the facade depicting historical events or victories. Top features an entablature with inscriptions. Some have multiple archways (one large central, two smaller side arches). Surface is smooth stone with carved details. Color is white, cream, or weathered gray. Positioned at the end of a grand avenue or in a public square.

Electric passenger bus drawing power from overhead wires via two trolley poles extending from the roof. Body is a long rectangular box (10-12 meters) with large windows along both sides. Roof-mounted trolley poles have carbon collector shoes that contact the wires. Entrance doors are at the front and/or middle. Interior has rows of seats and standing poles. Exterior is painted in transit authority colors with route numbers displayed. Front has a large windshield and destination sign. No exhaust pipe (zero emissions). Wheels are standard rubber tires on city streets.

Brass wind instrument with a long cylindrical tube bent into an elongated S-shape. Distinctive U-shaped slide mechanism allows the player to vary the tube length for pitch changes. Bell flares outward at the end (20-25 cm diameter). Mouthpiece is a cup-shaped brass piece inserted into the leadpipe. Surface is polished brass, gold brass, or silver-plated with a mirror-like reflective finish. Slide is made from two parallel tubes with inner and outer slides. Overall length approximately 2.7 meters when fully extended. Water key (spit valve) visible on the bell section.

Large open container with a wide circular or oval shape and vertical or slightly tapered sides. Diameter 40-100 cm, depth 30-60 cm. Material is wood (traditional washtub with metal bands), galvanized steel, plastic, or ceramic. Rim is rolled or reinforced for strength. Surface shows wear, scratches, or patina from use. Some tubs have handles on opposite sides. Interior may have measurement markings. Used for holding liquids, bathing, or storage. Wooden tubs show stave construction with metal hoops.

Access control gate consisting of a central vertical post with three or four rotating horizontal arms (tripod or full-height). Arms are metal tubes (chrome, stainless steel) extending 50-80 cm radially. Rotation is ratcheted to allow one person per push. Full-height turnstiles have a cage-like structure with vertical bars reaching 2+ meters. Base is bolted to the floor. Directional arrows indicate the flow of traffic. Some models have an electronic card reader or coin slot integrated into the post. Color is typically silver, black, or painted to match the facility.

Mechanical keyboard with rows of round or square keys arranged in a QWERTY layout. Each key has a raised letter/number/symbol printed on top. Keys are mounted on a flat or slightly curved keyboard plate. Key travel is deep with a tactile mechanical click. Frame is metal (cast iron or steel) painted black or gray. Space bar spans the bottom row. Shift keys are on either side. Carriage return lever is on the left side. Overall width approximately 30-40 cm. Keys show wear on frequently used characters. Typebars strike an inked ribbon from below.

Handheld collapsible canopy mounted on a central shaft with radiating ribs. Canopy is fabric (nylon, polyester) stretched over 6-8 metal or fiberglass ribs. When open, diameter is 90-120 cm. Shaft is metal or wood with a curved or straight handle. Collapsible models fold down to 25-35 cm via a telescoping shaft and folding ribs. Canopy colors range from solid black to vibrant patterns. Tip of each rib has a small protective cap. Opening mechanism is manual (push-up) or automatic (button-activated). Ribs converge at a runner that slides along the shaft.
